text: One on One is an American sitcom created by Eunetta T. Boone and aired on UPN from September 3, 2001, to May 15, 2006. The series stars Flex Alexander as a single sportscaster who becomes a full-time father when his ex-wife, Nicole Barnes (Tichina Arnold), takes a job in Nova Scotia and his teenage daughter Breanna Barnes (Kyla Pratt) moves in with him. Flex, who previously blew out his knee during an NBA game and used his communications degree—though he failed the class twice—to transition into sportscasting, works for the fictional WYNX-TV and lives in a luxury bachelor pad. He is a ladies' man who strives to be a responsible parent and best friend to Breanna, being very protective of her, especially from boys. His only serious relationship was with Nicole, whom he impregnated at 18. The show is set in Baltimore for the first four seasons before shifting to Los Angeles for the final season. It was a joint production of Greenblatt/Janollari Studio and Daddy's Girl Productions in association with Paramount Network Television, though it was not originally a Paramount production. The show was initially pitched to ABC in 1999 when the pilot was shot, but ABC declined due to declining sitcom audiences. It was then pitched to The WB, which passed on it because it wasn’t “teen enough,” and later to Fox Television Studios, which also declined due to it not fitting their financial model. After ABC, The WB, and Fox rejected the show, UPN executives took interest, especially due to the success of Moesha’s cancellation, and picked it up. Fox Television Studios dropped out last minute over financial concerns, prompting Paramount Television to step in. The series featured guest appearances from celebrities and athletes such as Lil' Zane, Chris Brown, Lil' Romeo, Eve, Lloyd, Floetry, Angie Stone, Mario, Omarion, Brandy, Solange Knowles, Nina Sky, Marques Houston, Smokey Robinson, Kim Fields, Avant, Jennifer Freeman, Nate Dogg, Bobby V, Claudia Jordan, Ruben Studdard, and Lisa Leslie. The show was cancelled months before UPN and The WB merged to form The CW. A spin-off series, Cuts, premiered as a mid-season replacement in the 2004–2005 season and followed Flex’s younger stepbrother Kevin Barnes running a barbershop/day spa with a spoiled brat named Tiffany Sherwood after her father Jack Sherwood purchased the shop. Cuts also lasted two seasons and was cancelled when UPN and The WB merged. The series centers on Flex Washington (Alexander) and his daughter Breanna Barnes (Pratt), beginning with Breanna wanting to stay with Flex, whom she previously saw only two weeks a year. Flex’s best friend and Breanna’s godfather, Duane Odell Knox (Kelly Perine), is a used-car salesman who lives across the hall and is a constant presence; he is often repelled by women, though his only serious girlfriend was Candy (Shondrella Avery), whom he dated for two years before breaking up. Breanna’s best friend is Spirit Jones (Sicily Sewell), with whom she creates mischief, and her other best friend, Arnaz Ballard (Robert Ri'chard), is the object of her on-again, off-again affection. Breanna becomes jealous of Arnaz’s old girlfriend, Ginger (Khanya Mkhize), and Arnaz becomes jealous when Breanna starts dating Josh (Josh Henderson). They eventually become a couple in the latter part of the series, break up in season 3, and later rekindle their relationship, ending with Arnaz chasing after Michelle (Brandy Norwood), D-Mack’s sister, while Breanna is shown in bed with D-Mack (Ray J). The show’s theme song, "Living One on One," was written and performed by Shanice (Flex Alexander’s wife) and Tonex, with music composed by Jonathan Wolff and Becky Kneubuhl, who also composed the scene-change music for the first season. For the fifth season, the theme was slightly shortened and remixed by Detail and Ray J, and a truncated version with only the words "One on One" was used as a closing theme in syndicated airings. The opening titles for the first three seasons featured the cast playing basketball on an outdoor court, with additional scenes showing Spirit checking out a boy and Arnaz playing guitar interrupted by a bouncing basketball. The fourth-season opening featured the cast in a dressing room preparing for a night out, ending with a pan shot of them in mirrors wearing different outfits. The first four seasons included a closeup of Flex, Breanna, and Arnaz before cutting to a shot of the entire cast. The final season’s opening showed the main cast (Breanna, Arnaz, D-Mack, Sara, Cash, and Lisa) at various locations on the Venice Beach Boardwalk before meeting at a beach house for a photo. The show began airing in syndication in September 2006, with CBS Paramount Domestic Television holding distribution rights for the first year, and CBS Media Ventures taking over since September 2007. In the U.S., it aired on local stations (mostly Fox, The CW, and MyNetworkTV) from September 2006 to September 2009, and was rerun on Noggin’s teen block, The N, starting in October 2006. It continued on The N after it became a 24-hour channel in December 2007, running until October 2008, then returned to The N on September 14, 2009, and moved to TeenNick on September 28, 2009, airing in two-hour morning and late-night blocks before being removed in 2013. The show aired on BET in 2009 in two one-hour blocks (one weekday morning and one afternoon) and on Saturdays. Formerly, Bounce TV and TV One also broadcast the series. It joined Netflix on October 15, 2020. As of 2024, reruns can be seen on Cleo TV and Dabl. Overseas, the series is broadcast in Canada on BET and local affiliates, in Australia on Nine Network, in South Africa on SABC1, and in the Middle East on the Paramount Comedy Channel (though the fifth season has not been aired in full). It is also broadcast across Africa via the Sony Entertainment Channel through DSTV.
